posts.title: Geely Auto lifts export goal to 920,000 as overseas becomes only growth engine
posts.summary:
The new target represents nearly 120% growth from 2025 exports, with the company targeting a combined 1,000,000-vehicle scale across 5 key overseas markets.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Auto has aggressively raised its 2026 export target to 920,000 vehicles, a 44% increase from its original goal and a 120% jump over 2025 levels.
The company is pivoting heavily toward international markets as a primary growth engine, following a 22.6% decline in domestic China sales during the first half of the year.
New energy vehicles (NEVs) are the primary catalyst for international expansion, with July NEV exports surging 616% year-on-year and representing 59% of total export volume.
Geely has identified five key geographic regions—ASEAN, Pan-Europe, Eastern Europe, Latin America/Africa, and the Middle East/Asia-Pacific—to support a total overseas scale of 1,000,000 vehicles.

posts.title: CATL says core operations carbon neutral by end-2025, supply chain next
posts.summary:
CATL said its supply chain accounts for more than 80% of its products' carbon emissions, and it aims to achieve value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: CATL has achieved carbon neutrality across its core operations as of the end of 2025, utilizing 100% zero-carbon electricity across its production facilities.
The company has set a new target to reach value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035, a critical step given that over 80% of its product lifecycle emissions originate from the supply chain.
CATL has implemented a full-chain carbon data traceability platform, the Carbon Chain Management System (CCMS), to monitor emissions from mineral extraction through component manufacturing.

Despite scaling production to 748 GWh in 2025, CATL reported a 77% reduction in carbon-emissions intensity over the last two years, demonstrating a decoupling of manufacturing growth from carbon output.

posts.title: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
posts.summary: Stripe is reportedly acquiring OpenRouter, an implicit bet on a future market of models and the chance at Aggregation.
bullets: Stripe's reported acquisition of OpenRouter signals a strategic pivot toward becoming a central aggregator in the fragmented AI model landscape.
By controlling the infrastructure layer for model access, Stripe aims to capture value from the proliferation of diverse AI models rather than relying solely on payment processing.
This move represents an attempt to flip the traditional business model by positioning Stripe as the essential middleware for developers integrating multiple AI services.
The acquisition suggests that Stripe views the future of software as being defined by model-agnostic workflows, where the platform that simplifies access to these models gains significant leverage.

posts.title: 800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid To Gate
posts.summary:
The next power bottleneck is no longer just inside the accelerator — it is the full conversion path from medium-voltage AC to sub-1V silicon.
The post 800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid To Gate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: AI data center power requirements are scaling rapidly, with server rack densities projected to increase from 125 kilowatts today to 1 megawatt in the near future.
The industry is shifting toward 800VDC architectures to minimize conversion losses as power moves from the medium-voltage grid to sub-1V silicon gates.
Transitioning to solid-state transformers is becoming critical to reduce the number of conversion stages, thereby improving thermal margins and overall system efficiency.
Component suppliers must fundamentally redesign power electronics to support these high-voltage architectures, moving away from traditional 12V or 48V distribution models.

posts.title: The Download: dead robot friends and the “censorship-industrial complex”
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. What happens when a kid’s robot best friend dies? When Xander first met Moxie, she taught him how to calm down when he was anxious or mad. Six years later, she…
bullets: The collapse of AI companion toy manufacturers, such as the maker of the Moxie robot, highlights significant consumer risks regarding hardware longevity and the reliance on centralized cloud servers for functionality.

The 'censorship-industrial complex' theory has transitioned from fringe political discourse to a central influence on US policy, potentially reshaping how government agencies interact with Big Tech platforms regarding content moderation.

The US government is actively pressuring international allies to align with its AI initiatives, signaling an escalating geopolitical strategy to isolate China's influence in the global artificial intelligence sector.

Beijing is increasingly leveraging open-weight AI models to enhance its governance capabilities, creating a strategic divide within the White House regarding the risks and benefits of open-source AI proliferation.
